content:
We just published our list of the 10 Best Small-Cap Value Stocks to Invest In Now , and Coursera, Inc. (NYSE:COUR) ranked 6th on the list.

The slide in AI stocks is prompting investors to explore beyond the market's leading companies. According to Reuters on November 2, more than 70% of S&P 500 constituents increased in October, despite steep drops in AI-related companies, while small- and mid-cap indexes also advanced. "Investors want to maintain equity exposure. But now they want to reduce AI concentration risk and are adding to areas that offer differentiated sources of return," said Angelo Kourkafas, senior global investment strategist at Edward Jones. This broadening opens up opportunities for smaller companies whose attractiveness is based on earnings and cash generation rather than enthusiasm for AI spending, a theme Insider Monkey explored in its coverage of Howard Marks' warnings on AI stocks .

On October 20, the Russell 2000 gained 1.7% and the S&P 500 Value Index jumped 0.9%, while the growth counterpart declined 0.2%. Speaking to Reuters, Jim Baird, chief investment officer at Plante Moran Financial Advisors, said the following:

"Equity investors are still a little skeptical around the AI trade and the ability for some of these companies to monetize their investments, so you're seeing a bit of a rotation into other areas of the market."

The shift strengthens the case for looking beyond crowded technology markets to other areas, such the smaller companies profiled in Insider Monkey's 10 Cheap Small Cap Stocks to Buy Now .

Small-cap value has also provided some safety during the recent slump. In his third-quarter review , Royce Investment Partners Co-Chief Investment Officer Francis Gannon noted that the Russell 2000 Value Index fell 4.9%, compared to the Russell 2000 Growth Index's 9.4% drop. That doesn't make value stocks immune to losses, but it shows why starting valuation is important when investors are less willing to pay for future growth.

Gannon claims that the opportunity hasn't disappeared following the rebound. "Today, we see a potentially powerful combination for small-cap investors: accelerating earnings, attractive relative valuations, and low expectations," he wrote in a commentary published on October 30. He emphasized higher-quality companies with robust balance sheets, sustained profitability, and disciplined capital allocation, a significant distinction between buying cheap businesses and simply buying declining share prices. That distinction also influences stock selection. In this regard, Insider Monkey's recent 10 Strong Buy Small Cap Stocks to Invest In provides a similar view on smaller companies receiving analyst support.

That said, the rotation still has limitations. Reuters warned that broader market weakness might transform diversification into outright risk reduction. "If the major averages begin to drop in a more compelling manner, it is very likely that investors will stop rotating into other sectors … and start rotating into cash," Miller Tabak's Matt Maley wrote in a note. The best small-cap value candidates need more than just a positive market trend: earnings, liquidity, and balance-sheet strength that can endure a less supportive environment.

We rated qualifying stocks based on hedge fund ownership, using Insider Monkey's Q2 2026 database. Coursera qualified with a forward PE ratio of 6.91 and a trailing revenue growth rate of 44.35%. Its 27 hedge fund holders ranked it sixth among the selected companies.

Coursera, Inc., operates an online learning platform and has owned Udemy since May 11. The company's revenue increased 94% to $376.7 million in the third quarter, however this was due to the consolidation of Udemy. Gross margin came in at 64%, with adjusted EBITDA of $61.5 million or a 16.3% margin. Management expects to achieve its $115 million annual net synergy target within eight months of completion, rather than the initial 24 months. It also unveiled Project Helix, an AI-native skills platform set to launch for enterprise customers in the first half of 2027.

The underlying picture is weak, as shares plunged nearly 19% following the report. Core subscription growth was more than offset by pressure on individual certificate subscriptions and Udemy's transactional products, resulting in a $25.6 million GAAP net loss. The fourth-quarter revenue projection of $358 million to $366 million is lower than the third quarter, indicating flat enterprise growth and ongoing consumer decline. Moreover, earlier this year, management predicted a 2% to 4% fall in revenue in 2026. That leaves the profitability as the central test: Coursera's lower sales multiple may look attractive next to competitor Duolingo's, but the discount only matters if it can turn its enlarged revenue base into sustainable earnings, a trade-off explored in Insider Monkey's comparison of Coursera and Duolingo .
